newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's EMU efforts could cause crisis -- Dornbusch.
newsitem.headline: Italy's EMU efforts could cause crisis -- Dornbusch.

text.p: Italy's efforts to become a founding member of European economic and monetary union (EMU) are doomed to failure and could trigger a currency crisis, Rudiger Dornbusch, economics professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, said Friday.

"Germany and France will form a currency union but on the way Italy and France will have an EMU crisis," Dornbusch told reporters at a three-day meeting of bankers, industrialists and academics at a lakeside resort in northern Italy.

Dornbusch said problems would start when financial markets realise that Italy's government, faced with a flagging economy, is unable to deliver a sufficiently tight 1997 budget to keep alive the country's chances of joining EMU in 1999.

"The crisis will start in Italy if the government can't get a significantly good (1997) budget and if the weak economic performance make the budget even weaker than expected. If that turns out to be true, by early next year Italy is clearly out of the prospect of European Monetary Union," said Dornbusch.
"If that happens the pressure moves over to France. A weak lira, higher Italian interest rates ... in France the question is: will they have enough stamina?", he added

"The French will raise interest rates, unemployment will rise. Clearly, France will suffer a crisis. I believe in the end France and Germany will have monetary union, but on the way from here to there first Italy and then France will have an EMU crisis," he added.
France would pay a high price for EMU membership. "France will get very badly bruised on the way there," said Dornbusch.

Italy was running a grave risk by closely identifying efforts to put its economic house in order with its race against time to meet the tough economic targets enshrined in the Maastricht Treaty which sets out the ground rules for EMU membership.

"It's a mistake for Italy to put an EMU label on something that Italy will have to do anyway," he said. "Italy's problems go far beyond the EMU criteria and keep your eye on those problems and don't be mesmerised by a bonus from EMU because it is isn't going to happen."
"Italy's problems need to be fixed. The danger is that the adjustment is discredited when you fail to get into EMU," said Dornbusch.
